message.content:
Read-only investigation in /opt/nxeon (Next.js + Prisma VPS hosting platform). Do NOT edit any file. I am writing internal documentation and need VERIFIED facts with real `file:line` citations (absolute paths). Be very thorough.

Investigate the BILLING subsystem and report:

1. `worker/billing.ts` — full behaviour. Renewal loop: how servers are selected for renewal, how the price is computed, wallet-credit-first then card-for-remainder logic, retry schedule (days 1/3/5), dunning emails, what happens on final failure, suspension. Cite line numbers for each stage. Quote the exact retry-day logic and the exact function names.
2. `Server.suspendReason` — every value used (UNPAID / ABUSE / ADMIN etc.), where each is set and where each is read, and what behaviour differs per value (e.g. can the customer unsuspend themselves? does paying an invoice auto-resume?). grep across the whole repo.
3. `lib/proration.ts` — the single shared function: signature, exact formula, rounding, who calls it (grep all callers with file:line). Confirm the claim "displayed = charged = credited".
4. `lib/resize.ts` — resize flow, upgrade vs downgrade, credit handling, how it uses proration, what job it enqueues.
5. Wallet + checkout + the wallet/card split: `lib/order.ts`, `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`, `lib/stripe.ts`, `lib/stripe-cards.ts`, `lib/actions-billing.ts`, `lib/actions-payment-method.ts`, `app/api/stripe/*`. Explain exactly how a purchase decides wallet vs card vs split, idempotency, and where the WalletTxn/Invoice rows are written.
6. Invoices: `lib/invoices.ts` — numbering, PDF/HTML rendering, statuses, who can view, the API route.
7. Plans / terms / pricing: `lib/billing-terms.ts`, `lib/product-billing.ts`, `lib/promotions.ts`, the Plan model, term multipliers/discounts, where prices are displayed vs charged.
8. `worker/product-renewals.ts` — what it renews, how it differs from worker/billing.ts.

For each: name failure modes you can actually see in the code (error paths, throws, catch blocks that swallow), and anything that is written-but-never-read or simulated/stubbed (very important — the codebase has a known overclaiming problem). Report concisely but with every citation as /opt/nxeon/path:line.

model Plan {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  slug          String   @unique
  name          String
  cpuCores      Int
  ramMB         Int
  diskGB        Int
  bandwidthTB   Float    @default(1)
  priceCents    Int
  storageTier   String   @default("nvme") // "nvme" | "hdd"
  active        Boolean  @default(true)
  sortOrder     Int      @default(0)
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  servers       Server[]
  gamePlans     GamePlan[]
}

enum ImageCategory {
  PLAIN_OS
  CONTROL_PANEL
  APPLICATION
}

/// An installable image shown in the deploy wizard. Plain OS clones `baseVmid`
/// directly; control panels / apps clone `baseVmid` then run `setupScript`
/// (cloud-init runcmd) to install the panel/app on first boot.
model OsTemplate {
  id            String        @id @default(cuid())
  slug          String        @unique
  name          String        // display name, e.g. "Ubuntu"
  category      ImageCategory @default(PLAIN_OS)
  family        String        @default("linux") // ubuntu | debian | almalinux | rocky | cpanel | ...
  version       String        @default("")      // "24.04", "13", ""
  logo          String        @default("")      // icon slug for the UI
  vmid          Int           // legacy/base template VMID to clone
  baseVmid      Int?          // explicit base OS template for panels/apps (falls back to vmid)
  setupScript   String?       // shell installed via cloud-init runcmd (panels/apps)
  minRamMB      Int           @default(1024)
  minDiskGB     Int           @default(10)
  licenseRequired Boolean     @default(false)   // e.g. cPanel/Plesk need a paid license
  featured      Boolean       @default(false)
  sortOrder     Int           @default(0)
  active        Boolean       @default(true)
  servers       Server[]
}

model Server {
model Server {
  id            String       @id @default(cuid())
  id            String       @id @default(cuid())
  name          String
  label         String?      // customer-facing nickname (rename)
  hostname      String
  vmid          Int?         @unique
  status        ServerStatus @default(PENDING)
  ipAddress     String?      @unique
  sshPort       Int?         @unique
  rootPassword  String?
  rootPasswordEnc String?
  isFree        Boolean      @default(false)
  autoRenew     Boolean      @default(true)
  gameVariant   String?      // game-server type/loader (e.g. paper, carbon, bepinex) — see lib/game-config
  gameConfig    Json?        // per-game settings values (validated against the family schema)
  suspendedNote String?
  // WHY a server is suspended: "UNPAID" | "ABUSE" | "ADMIN". Null = never suspended.
  //
  // `suspendedNote` used to be the only signal, and nothing consumed it, so every
  // suspension looked identical to the billing engine. Two live consequences:
  // (1) `terminateOverdue` selected on `status: "SUSPENDED"` alone, while the
  //     renewal sweep EXCLUDES suspended servers — so an admin suspending a
  //     paid-up customer pending an investigation meant they were never charged,
  //     never warned, their term lapsed, and 13 days later their VM and all its
  //     data were destroyed with a "prolonged non-payment" notice they had never
  //     been given a chance to act on.
  // (2) `renewNow` auto-unsuspended ANY suspended server on payment, so a spammer
  //     suspended for outbound abuse could pay and put themselves straight back
  //     on the network.
  // Both now scope strictly to UNPAID.
  suspendReason String?
  expiresAt     DateTime?
  // ---- Dunning (failed auto-charge retry state) ----
  // dunningStage counts CARD ATTEMPTS THAT HAVE FAILED for the current unpaid
  // period: 0 = nothing owed / paid, 1..N = that many failures. Reset to 0 the
  // moment a renewal succeeds. `dunningNextAt` gates the next retry so a
  // 5-minute billing sweep cannot burn every retry in a quarter of an hour, and
  // `dunningPayUrl` is a hosted Checkout link emailed to the customer so they can
  // clear the balance themselves (also how 3-D Secure challenges are satisfied).
  dunningStage  Int          @default(0)
  dunningNextAt DateTime?
  dunningPayUrl String?
  createdAt     DateTime     @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime     @updatedAt
  userId        String
  user          User         @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  nodeId        String?
  node          Node?        @relation(fields: [nodeId], references: [id])
  bwInBytes     BigInt       @default(0)
  bwOutBytes    BigInt       @default(0)
  abuseBwMark   BigInt?      // last bwOutBytes sample, for outbound-rate abuse detection
  abuseBwMarkAt DateTime?    // when abuseBwMark was taken
  bwWindowStart DateTime     @default(now())
  termMonths    Int          @default(1) // 1=monthly, 12=annual, 24=biennial, 36=triennial
  /// GB of root disk purchased BEYOND the plan's `diskGB`. The server's EFFECTIVE
  /// disk is always `plan.diskGB + extraDiskGB`, so the extra survives a plan
  /// resize (it is additive to whichever plan the server sits on). Growth is
  /// ONE-WAY: shrinking a live filesystem risks data loss, so nothing anywhere
  /// in the platform ever decrements this field.
  extraDiskGB   Int          @default(0)
  addons        Json         @default("{}") // { malwareScanner, dailyBackup, docker }
  dedicatedIp   DedicatedIp?
  wantsDedicatedIp Boolean   @default(false)
  projectId     String?
  project       Project?     @relation(fields: [projectId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  planId        String
  plan          Plan         @relation(fields: [planId], references: [id])
  osTemplateId  String
  osTemplate    OsTemplate   @relation(fields: [osTemplateId], references: [id])
  jobs          Job[]
  portForwards  PortForward[]
  autoUpdate    Boolean      @default(false) // game-server auto-update opt-in
  claudeBuilds  ClaudeBuild[]
  gamePlanId    String?
  gamePlan      GamePlan?    @relation(fields: [gamePlanId], references: [id])
  ipv6          String?      // assigned IPv6 address
  autoBackup    Boolean      @default(false)
  backupIntervalHours Int?   // scheduled-backup cadence
  lastAutoBackup DateTime?
  volumes       Volume[]
  websites      Website[]
  vpsDatabases  VpsDatabase[]
  appInstalls   AppInstall[]
  cronJobs      CronJob[]
}

model PortForward {
  id         String  @id @default(cuid())
  serverId   String
  server     Server  @relation(fields: [serverId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

model Job {
  id        String    @id @default(cuid())

createdAt DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime  @updatedAt

/// `stripeSessionId` is UNIQUE: it is the idempotency key that makes crediting a
/// Checkout session safe against concurrent confirm-redirect + webhook delivery.
model WalletTransaction {
  stripeSessionId String? @unique
  // Same role as stripeSessionId but for OFF-SESSION renewal charges, which have
  // no Checkout session. The UNIQUE constraint — not a read-then-write check — is
  // what makes crediting an auto-charge idempotent when a sweep retries.
  stripePaymentIntentId String? @unique
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId      String
  user        User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  amountCents Int
  description String
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
}

model AuditLog {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String?
  user      User?    @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
}

model Setting {

  value String

enum DedicatedIpStatus {
  FREE
  PAID
  VOID
  REFUNDED
}

model Invoice {
  id          String        @id @default(cuid())
  number      Int           @unique @default(autoincrement())
  userId      String
  user        User          @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  amountCents Int
  taxCents    Int           @default(0)
  status      InvoiceStatus @default(OPEN)
  // How much of this invoice has already been refunded. Refunds used to be bound
  // to nothing: `refundPayment` took only (userId, amount) and picked its Stripe
  // target as "most recent top-up, any amount" — so refunding a $24 March invoice
  // issued $24 against the customer's $200 July top-up, the invoice stayed PAID,
  // and the next admin refunded it again. Tracking it here lets the action refuse
  // to exceed the original and mark the invoice REFUNDED.
  refundedCents Int         @default(0)
  description String
  lineItems   Json          // [{ description, qty, unitCents, amountCents }]
  periodStart DateTime?
  periodEnd   DateTime?
  paidAt      DateTime?
  createdAt   DateTime      @default(now())
}

// ---- Growth: coupons / promo codes ----
enum CouponKind {
  PERCENT      // value = percent 1-100 (discount on order/topup)
  FIXED_CENTS  // value = cents off
